tissue-viability-and-wound-care.org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
tissue-viability-and-wound-care.title: Pressure ulcers: prevention and management (CG179)
tissue-viability-and-wound-care.fact: Covers risk assessment, prevention and treatment for children, young people and adults at risk of, or with, a pressure ulcer, in secondary and tertiary care and in primary care, community care and emergency departments. On mattresses its recommendations say: use a high-specification foam mattress for adults admitted to secondary care or assessed as high risk in primary and community care (1.1.13); for adults with a pressure ulcer, use high-specification foam and, if that is not sufficient to redistribute pressure, consider a dynamic support surface (1.4.9); do not use standard-specification foam for adults with a pressure ulcer (1.4.10). Adults at high risk should change position at least every 4 hours (1.1.9). NICE last reviewed the guideline on 30 November 2018 and found no new evidence affecting the recommendations.
tissue-viability-and-wound-care.quote: We have found no new evidence that affects the recommendations.
tissue-viability-and-wound-care.use: Recommendation 1.4.9 is the line for any dynamic or moving mattress: NICE says to consider a dynamic support surface when high-specification foam is not enough for someone with a pressure ulcer.

Statement 9, on medical device-related pressure ulcers, is a placeholder. It applies in England and Wales.
tissue-viability-and-wound-care.use: Statement 8 is the measurable standard a trust's mattress and cushion provision can be audited against.

tissue-viability-and-wound-care.title: Implementing the pressure ulcer framework in local reporting systems and reporting to NRLS
tissue-viability-and-wound-care.date: Not dated on the document (held in NHS England's September 2021 uploads)
tissue-viability-and-wound-care.fact: A guide for tissue viability nurses and pressure ulcer prevention leads on putting the 'Pressure ulcers: revised definition and measurement framework' into local incident reporting. The recommendations it lists include: the Department of Health and Social Care definition of avoidable/unavoidable should not be used; the 72-hour rule should be abandoned; pressure ulcers of grade 2 and above (the guide's wording) present on admission, and unstageable ulcers, should be included in local monitoring; moisture-associated skin damage should be counted alongside. Where pressure-relieving equipment failed or was unavailable but no ulcer occurred, the incident is reported under a separate listing, not as a medical device related pressure ulcer. It is written for the National Reporting and Learning System (NRLS); whether NRLS is still the national route was not verified here.
tissue-viability-and-wound-care.quote: Pressure ulcer categories should not be linked to a specific preset degree of harm
tissue-viability-and-wound-care.use: How a trust counts pressure harm, which is the baseline a business case for a new surface has to move.

tissue-viability-and-wound-care.title: Cohort study evaluating the burden of wounds to the UK's National Health Service in 2017/2018: update from 2012/2013
tissue-viability-and-wound-care.fact: Estimates, from a sample of 3,000 patients' records, 202,000 recorded pressure ulcers in 2017/18, equivalent to 0.4% of the adult population. The annual NHS cost of managing all wounds was £8.3 billion, 81% of it incurred in the community. The healing rate of pressure ulcers was 43% higher, in relative terms, than in 2012/13, and patients with a pressure ulcer had a nursing visit or dressing change every 3 to 4 days. A pressure-ulcer-only cost figure was not checked here.
tissue-viability-and-wound-care.quote: There were an estimated 202 000 recorded pressure ulcers in the study year
tissue-viability-and-wound-care.use: A citable national volume (2017/18) for the cost-of-problem and frequency lines of a value case.

tissue-viability-and-wound-care.title: Prevention and management of pressure ulcers standards
tissue-viability-and-wound-care.fact: Apply across health and social care in Scotland to anyone at risk of, or with, a pressure ulcer, including primary and secondary care, hospices, independent clinics, care at home and care homes. The standards cover organisational leadership, staff education and training, information for people, initial risk assessment at admission or first contact, regular reassessment and a person-centred care plan.

emergency-and-urgent-care.title: Relationship between time spent in emergency departments, employment, and hospitalisation, England: 2021 to 2025
emergency-and-urgent-care.fact: Among working-age employees who attended a type 1 emergency department (ED) in England between April 2021 and March 2023, 37.0% were hospitalised more than one day after leaving the ED and 21.9% left employment within two years. After adjusting for clinical and demographic factors, later hospital admission was 6.0% higher for two to under four hours in the ED and 95.0% higher for 12 hours or more, compared with under two hours. ONS states these are associations, not causal relationships.
emergency-and-urgent-care.quote: this was 95.0% higher for individuals who spent 12 hours or more in the ED, compared with those who spent under two hours in the ED
emergency-and-urgent-care.use: Official evidence that long ED stays go with later admissions, for a flow, triage or discharge conversation. Associations only: do not say long waits cause admissions.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: Musculoskeletal elective treatment waiting times and labour market outcomes, England: 2014 to 2025
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: Among working-age NHS patients having elective inpatient treatment for musculoskeletal (MSK) pain in England between April 2015 and March 2023, each extra four weeks of waiting reduced annual earnings by up to £487 (other joint disorders), £392 (other MSK conditions), £329 (back, neck and MSK pain) and £301 (osteoarthritis). ONS found no statistical evidence of a link between waiting time and later employment status or benefit receipt.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: each additional four weeks of waiting led to a £487 reduction in annual earnings in the fourth year after treatment
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: A cost-of-waiting figure for elective orthopaedic recovery and theatre throughput conversations.

Requirements stated for future tenders include ISO 9001:2015 or ISO 13485:2016 (or Medical Device Single Audit Program) certification, a Modern Slavery Assessment Tool score of 41% or above, Evergreen Level 1 and, where patient data or IT is handled, Cyber Essentials Plus.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: The planned publication date has changed from 7th October 2026 to 19th October 2026.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: Surgical Navigation Systems with Associated Options and Related Services
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: Reference 2021/S 000-007768, 72 months from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2028 (an initial 24-month extension followed by a further 24-month extension). orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Purchase of Orthopaedic Trauma & Extremity Implants & Consumables
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: Scotland buys trauma and extremity implants through its own national contract, not TOS3. Ceiling prices apply on eight lots.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: Purchase of Orthopaedic Spinal & Scoliosis Implants & Consumables

orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Purchase of Orthopaedic Spinal & Scoliosis Implants & Consumables

orthopaedics-and-trauma.org: Business Services Organisation (BSO) Procurement and Logistics Service
orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: Orthopaedics - Hip and Knee Replacement Products
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: Contract details notice 2026/S 000-090220, published 23 September 2026, for the four Health and Social Care trusts that are Other organisations on the notice (Belfast, Western, Southern, South Eastern). Four contracts, all signed 1 September 2026: Hip Implants (standard), 3 suppliers, £15,750,000 excluding VAT; Knee Implants (standard), 2 suppliers, £15,750,000; Specialist Hips (bespoke and custom), 6 suppliers, £6,750,000; Specialist Knees, 5 suppliers, £6,750,000. orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Framework lot values may be shared with other lots

orthopaedics-and-trauma.org: Business Services Organisation (BSO) Procurement and Logistics Service
orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: Orthopaedics - Trauma and Joint Replacement Products
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: Contract details notice 2026/S 000-090225, published 23 September 2026, one contract with 24 suppliers, £105,000,000 excluding VAT, 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2028, for the same four Health and Social Care trusts. Suppliers named: Acumed, Adler Ortho UK, Armstrong Medical, ASFM t/a Advance Medical Supplies, Biocomposites, Bone Support UK, Causeway Surgical, ConMed UK, Down Surgical, Electramed, Fannin (NI), Hospital Innovations, Ideal Med, Integra Neurosciences, Johnson & Johnson Medical, Joint Operations, Link Orthopaedics UK, Lynch Medical Supplies, New Vision Healthcare, OrthoPediatrics EU, PEI Surgical, Stryker UK, Uniphar Medtech and Zimmer Biomet UK.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Supply of Implants and Consumables for use in Orthopaedic Trauma and Joint Replacement Surgery.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: The widest Northern Ireland route: 24 suppliers on one framework, against six for hip and knee.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: All Wales Orthopaedic, Trauma and Joint Replacement Framework
orthopaedics-and-trauma.ends: 31/01/2026 per the May 2025 notice; later status not verified
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: Modification notice 2025/S 000-027654, published 27 May 2025, lists 61 suppliers and a total value of £141,950,000 excluding VAT. Ten lots: Primary and Revision Hip; Primary and Revision Knee; Extremities Arthroplasty; Trauma/Maxillofacial; Spinal; Arthroscopy Products; Bone Preparation; Orthopaedic Power Tools and Consumables; Biologics; Value-Based Procurement & Innovation. It started 1 August 2021 and NWSSP extended it to 31 January 2026 'to facilitate a redesign of approach to market'. A February 2026 Cardiff and Vale award still refers to the All Wales Framework. What replaced it after 31 January 2026 is not verified: no later framework notice was found in this check.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership intends to extend the current agreement until 31st January 2026.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: Wales had a ten-lot national framework with 61 suppliers. Its successor route is not verified, so ask NWSSP before assuming one.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.org: Cardiff and Vale University Health Board (via NWSSP)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: Cardiff and Vale Knee Contract: four-year sole supply commitment to Zimmer Biomet
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: Contract award notice 2026/S 000-021902, published 11 March 2026, contract concluded 20 February 2026. Cardiff and Vale University Health Board entered a four-year sole supply commitment for knee implants with Zimmer Biomet UK Limited, covering approximately 80% of knee procedures via the All Wales Framework, valued at £3,384,842 excluding VAT. One tender was received.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: four-year sole supply commitment for knee implants with Zimmer Biomet
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: An example of a Welsh health board committing about 80% of knee volume to one supplier through the national framework.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: HTG743: Robot-assisted surgery for orthopaedic procedures, early value assessment
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: Six technologies can be used in the NHS during the evidence generation period as options for robot-assisted knee or hip replacement: ApolloKnee, CORI, Mako SmartRobotics, ROSA Knee, SkyWalker and VELYS. Use is conditional on evidence being generated under NICE's evidence generation plan and on regulatory approval including NHS England's Digital Technology Assessment Criteria (DTAC) approval. The evidence generation period is 3 years, after which NICE will assess whether routine adoption is appropriate. NICE has renumbered the content from Health technology evaluation 22 to HealthTech guidance 743, unchanged.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Six technologies can be used in the NHS during the evidence generation period as options for robot-assisted surgery for knee or hip replacements.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: Robot-assisted knee and hip surgery is allowed only while evidence is generated. A rep selling a robot needs to know the evidence plan commitments.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.org: Getting It Right First Time (GIRFT) and British Orthopaedic Association (BOA)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: Five high-volume, low-complexity (HVLC) orthopaedic pathways updated
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: GIRFT updated five national elective pathways with the BOA and specialist societies: total primary hip replacement; total and unicompartmental primary knee replacement; Dupuytren's disease; shoulder arthroscopy for rotator cuff repair or subacromial decompression; hallux valgus and rigidus. First issued in 2020. The 2026 updates align the follow-up sections with GIRFT's Further Faster Follow-Up Protocols and Standardising Follow-Up guidance. A joint GIRFT and BOA webinar is on 13 October 2026, 1pm to 2pm.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: it is imperative that all teams across England adopt them
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: The pathways set how clinics and theatres are run for the five highest-volume elective procedures, which shapes what trusts buy and when.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.org: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: MHRA orthopaedic Device Safety Information (DSI) since 2024
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: GOV.UK's Device Safety Information list tagged Orthopaedics returns these implant items: DSI/2026/010 Cobalt-chrome modular neck hip replacements (26 August 2026); DSI/2026/001 M6-C Artificial Cervical Disc, Spinal Kinetics, new monitoring for osteolysis (15 January 2026); DSI/2025/005 Profemur cobalt chrome modular neck hip replacements (4 September 2025); DSI/2024/007 CPT Hip System femoral stem 12/14 neck taper, periprosthetic femoral fracture (4 September 2024); DSI/2024/005 Symbios ORIGIN posterior stabilised patient-matched total knee, early revision (23 April 2024); DSI/2024/002 MAGEC X System, UK suspension lifted (12 March 2024). The same list holds one non-implant item, DSI/2026/003 on blood transfusion giving sets.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Cobalt-chrome modular neck hip replacements: risk of metal-wear effects and revision surgery (DSI/2026/010)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: A standing list of recent implant safety actions a rep can be asked about at any trust.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.org: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: DSI/2026/010: cobalt-chrome modular neck hip replacements, all withdrawn before 2019
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: An MHRA investigation of every hip replacement with a cobalt-chrome modular neck ever sold in the UK found increased wear and corrosion risk and a possible increase in revision for adverse local tissue reaction. All of these devices were removed from the market before 2019 and none remain commercially available. MHRA advises trusts to use the National Joint Registry (NJR) and local records to identify patients and invite them for virtual or face-to-face review; symptomatic patients annually, asymptomatic patients on a patient-initiated follow-up pathway. Table 1 (NJR data extracted June 2026) covers Aesculap Metha modular, LimaCorporate H-Max-M, Smith and Nephew SMF, Stryker ABG II modular and Symbios HARMONY modular and SPS modular. The advice for distributors is that there is none.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: there is no advice for distributors regarding this DSI
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: This is a patient-recall workload for trusts, not a product-switching event: the devices are off the market and distributors have no action. Do not frame it as a competitor opening.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: NJR 23rd Annual Report 2026: hips, knees and robotic use (surgical data to 31 December 2025)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: Primary hip replacements using unipolar implants reached 113,472 in 2025, a record for the fourth year running. Primary knee replacements reached a record 143,972 in 2025; NHS-funded procedures in NHS facilities have plateaued and now represent less than 50% of knee volume, against over 60% historically. Robotic procedures recorded in 2025: 3,762 hip and 11,641 knee. Mako was the most-used knee system (7,869) followed by CORI (1,590); CORI use roughly doubled since 2023; VELYS had its first recorded use in 2024; six knee systems have data recorded. Robotic hip replacement rose from 2,854 in 2023 to 3,762 in 2025.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: ANNUAL REPORT 2026
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: Current national volumes and the robotics share for sizing a hip or knee patch. The NJR does not publish a market-size value.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: Referral to Treatment (RTT) waiting times: Trauma and Orthopaedic Service (C_110) by trust
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: NHS England publishes monthly RTT provider files by treatment function; the latest on the 2026-27 page is July 2026. In the July 2026 full extract, Trauma and Orthopaedic Service is treatment function code C_110, with rows for completed admitted and non-admitted pathways, incomplete pathways, incomplete pathways with a decision to admit, and new RTT periods, at provider and commissioner level. This entry gives the source only; it states no waiting-list total.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Incomplete pathways are waiting times for cases where patients are still waiting to start treatment at the end of the month.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: The standing source for trust-level orthopaedic waiting pressure. Pull the C_110 rows for a named trust before quoting any figure.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: GIRFT Orthopaedic Surgery workstream: reports, pathways and news
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: GIRFT's Orthopaedic Surgery page describes two published reports (2015 and a February 2020 follow-up) and names Professor Tim Briggs as clinical lead. The 2020 follow-up headline findings include a reduction in revision rates every year since 2012 and a 20% reduction in average length of stay, releasing more than 368,000 bed days. The site is behind a bot check, so scripts cannot read it, but a normal browser can.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: A reduction in revision rates every year since 2012
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: The entry point for GIRFT's orthopaedic pathways and news. Trust-level GIRFT data is not public.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: TOS3 Supplier Matrix by Lot (issued 24 March 2025): who can sell on each sub-lot
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: The matrix has 99 supplier rows. Suppliers marked per lot: 1.1 Hips 22; 1.2 Knees 21; 1.3 Extremities Arthroplasty 22; 1.4 Complex Arthroplasty 18; 1.5 Internal and External Fixation 32; 1.6 Spine 26; 1.7 Arthroscopy / Sports Medicine 20; 1.8 Bone Preparation 19; 1.9 Power Tools Consumables 20; 1.10 Regenerative Technology 30; 1.11 Orthopaedic Additional Devices 26; 1.12 Custom/Customisable Implants 20; Lot 2 Equipment 36; Lot 3 Services and Solutions 22. NHS Supply Chain's own TOS3 page lists 101 awarded supplier names, so the matrix (issued March 2025) and the page do not match; which two names are absent from the matrix is not established here.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Total Orthopaedic Solutions 3 - Supplier Matrix by Lot
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: Shows how many competitors sit on each sub-lot, for example 32 on fixation against 18 on complex arthroplasty. Use the page, not this matrix, for the current supplier list.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: TOS3 Customer Engagement Guide: what Lots 2 and 3 cover
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: Lot 2 Equipment includes, but is not limited to: robotics, navigation, imaging, fluid management, consoles and arthroscopic stack systems, power tools, helmets (hoods/togas), tourniquet machines, bone harvesting/milling, ultrasound cement removal, cement mixing and ultrasound bone healing; consumables for equipment are in sub-lot 1.11. Lot 3 Services and Solutions includes, but is not limited to: wearable devices, patient/surgeon applications, software solutions, virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) technology, efficiency programmes, patient planning, managed equipment services and technical support.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: The consumables for equipment are found within sub lot 1.11.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: The authoritative list of what counts as equipment and services on TOS3. It is wider than the shorthand 'robotics, navigation, power tools'.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: TOS4 pipeline notice 2026/S 000-016123: the earlier notice, with a superseded tender date
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: The UK1 pipeline notice 'Musculoskeletal Surgical 2028 (Total Orthopaedic Solutions)', published 23 February 2026, shares its procurement identifier (ocds-h6vhtk-065a3d) with the UK2 engagement notice 2026/S 000-081660. It gave an estimated tender notice publication date of 1 November 2026, estimated value £3,000,000,000 excluding VAT, and contract dates 1 February 2028 to 31 January 2030 with a possible extension to 31 January 2032. The later notice moved the planned date to 19 October 2026. Any list still showing 1 November 2026, including the Hub's own NHS Supply Chain procurement calendar file, is using the older date.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Publication date of tender notice (estimated)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: Explains why two dates are in circulation. The 19 October 2026 date is the later one.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: SBS10238 Surgical Robots, Consumables and Related Services: a separate robotics route that names orthopaedics
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: Framework SBS10238 is active 24 May 2023 to 23 May 2027 and open to all NHS organisations in the UK. Its page lists orthopaedics among the specialties surgical robots serve (with urology, colorectal and gynaecology). It allows a further competition or direct award under Regulation 33 of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015. Three suppliers are named: CMR Surgical Limited, Intuitive Surgical Ltd and Medtronic. The page does not say which of them supply orthopaedic systems, so whether the framework is a route for hip or knee robots is not verified. TOS3 Lot 2 also lists robotics.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Via this framework agreement, you can run a further competition, or choose to direct award to a supplier
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: A second robotics route exists outside TOS3. Check with SBS which of its three suppliers cover orthopaedic systems before telling a trust it is an option.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: Contracts Finder: where trust TOS3 call-offs are published
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: The Kettering, Northampton and Oxford TOS3 call-offs cited in this list were published on Contracts Finder as 'Call-off from a framework agreement' notices, each carrying contract start and end dates and a value. The search page accepts keywords across contract title, description and buyer. Search for 'TOS3' and for 'Lot 1.' (sub-lot numbers) to find further call-offs.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Can include contract title, description and buyer
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: The place to find which trust has called off which TOS3 sub-lot, and when the call-off ends.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.org: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: MHRA weekly Field Safety Notices page
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: MHRA publishes manufacturers' Field Safety Notices (FSNs) as one page a week. The latest at this check is 'Field Safety Notices: 21 to 25 September 2026', published 29 September 2026. Entries give manufacturer, product, date and MHRA reference and are not tagged by device type; the page includes, for example, F.H. Industrie CALCANAIL threaded cannulated screw (5 September 2026). MHRA says it publishes them for information only and a recipient must act on a notice from the manufacturer.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: If you receive a field safety notice (FSN) from a manufacturer you must always act on it.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: Where a recall or correction on an orthopaedic product first appears publicly. Scan by manufacturer name each week.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: ODEP product ratings: hip, knee and other implants
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: ODEP's products page lists rated implant components with component name, material and a 'Next ODEP Review Due' field, searchable by supplier and filterable by rating. The site also has pages for Beyond Compliance implants, digital certificates and procurement. Ratings are not restated here; read the entry for the product concerned.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Next ODEP Review Due
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: A surgeon or procurement lead will ask for an implant's ODEP rating. Check the product's entry and its review due date before a conversation.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: NHFD 2026 annual report, 'Mind the Gap', and live key performance indicators
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: The 2026 NHFD annual report, on 2025 data, was published 10 September 2026 and highlights continued variation in hip fracture care across hospitals. The key performance indicator page, annualised on 70,699 cases to the end of August 2026, shows: admission to specialist ward 10%; prompt orthogeriatric review 90%; prompt surgery 57%; NICE-compliant surgery 71%; promptly out of bed 82%; not delirious post-operatively 68%; return to original residence 75%; bone medication 62%.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: NHFD Report 2026 (10 September 2026)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: National benchmarks for hip fracture care, relevant to trauma implants and orthogeriatric pathway conversations.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: Hospital Admitted Patient Care Activity 2025-26: procedure and provider tables
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: The 2025-26 publication covers 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026 and records 22.6 million finished consultant episodes, up 71,455 (0.3%) on 2024-25. Downloads on the page include a procedures-and-interventions table, a provider table (hospital trusts) and a specialty table. Procedure counts are by operation code, so each code must be matched to a named procedure before a figure is quoted; this entry states no orthopaedic count.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: In 2025-26 there were 22.6 million FCEs recorded.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: The source for national and trust procedure volumes by operation code once the codes are mapped.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: GIRFT surgical hub accreditation: 83 hubs by June 2026, 125 in operation
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: At cohort 12 (announced 1 June 2026) the total accredited since March 2023 was 83. GIRFT runs quarterly cohorts aiming to accredit all 125 hubs in operation in England. The scheme is run with the Royal College of Surgeons and supported by the Royal College of Anaesthetists. Hubs focus on high-volume, low-complexity surgery including trauma and orthopaedics (including spinal surgery). Cohort 12's hubs include the Essex and Suffolk Elective Orthopaedic Centre, Pontefract Hospital Elective Orthopaedic Centre and Hampshire Elective Orthopaedic Centre. Earlier cohort announcements are on the same site.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: GIRFT is running quarterly cohorts to accredit all 125 hubs currently in operation across the NHS in England.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: Surgical hubs are where much elective orthopaedic volume is moving. This names accredited orthopaedic centres and the programme's target.

pain-management.title: Musculoskeletal elective treatment waiting times and labour market outcomes, England: 2014 to 2025
pain-management.fact: Among working-age NHS patients having elective inpatient treatment for musculoskeletal (MSK) pain in England between April 2015 and March 2023, each extra four weeks of waiting reduced annual earnings by up to £487 (other joint disorders), £392 (other MSK conditions), £329 (back, neck and MSK pain) and £301 (osteoarthritis). ONS found no statistical evidence of a link between waiting time and later employment status or benefit receipt.
pain-management.quote: For patients with "back, neck and MSK pain", the largest reduction in annual earnings for each additional four weeks of waiting time was of £329, in the third year after treatment
pain-management.use: A cost-of-waiting figure for back, neck and MSK pain pathway conversations.

frailty-and-older-people.title: Deaths registered in England and Wales: 2025
frailty-and-older-people.fact: 570,988 deaths were registered in England and Wales in 2025, 0.4% more than in 2024. Dementia and Alzheimer's disease was the leading cause, with 72,272 deaths (12.7% of all deaths): 16.5% of female deaths and 9.1% of male deaths. The age-standardised mortality rate was 913 per 100,000, the lowest since the series began in 1994. The North East had the highest age-standardised rates in England for both males (1,189) and females (880).
frailty-and-older-people.quote: Dementia and Alzheimer's disease continued to be the leading cause of death in England and Wales, with 72,272 deaths registered (12.7% of all deaths)
frailty-and-older-people.use: Scale of dementia as the leading cause of death, and where mortality is highest, for older-people and care-setting conversations.

cardiology-and-cardiac-surgery.title: Deaths registered in England and Wales: 2025
cardiology-and-cardiac-surgery.fact: Ischaemic heart diseases were the leading cause of death among males in England and Wales in 2025, accounting for 12.2% of male deaths registered. Across all deaths, the leading cause was dementia and Alzheimer's disease (12.7%).
cardiology-and-cardiac-surgery.quote: Among males, ischaemic heart diseases were the leading cause of death, accounting for 12.2% of deaths registered in 2025.
cardiology-and-cardiac-surgery.use: Headline burden figure for coronary heart disease in men.

patient-handling.title: Pressure Area Care and Patient Handling (2025/S 000-086469)
patient-handling.fact: Runs 24 months from 9 March 2026 to 8 March 2028, with an option to extend for a further 24 months. 53 suppliers, 10 of them new, across three lots: Lot 1 beds, mattresses, pressure reducing products and manual handling equipment; Lot 2 managed service for beds and mattresses; Lot 3 rental and decontamination. 982 new products were added. NHS Supply Chain says products are clinically assured through its clinical evaluation process, which the page calls CaPA.
patient-handling.use: The national route for mattresses and pressure-reducing products until at least March 2028. NHS Innovation Service guidance says new suppliers cannot be added to an agreed framework, so a supplier not on it should expect trust tenders, other frameworks and the re-let.

patient-handling.title: NHS procurement frameworks (innovation guide)
patient-handling.fact: States that new suppliers cannot be added to an agreed procurement framework, except a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS). The Medical Technology DPS for Innovative Products (Innovation DPS) is open to innovations submitted to the NHS Innovation Service and accepted by NHS Supply Chain, or referred to NHS Supply Chain by the HIN (as the page names it), and the technology must meet national policy objectives and have a National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) recommendation. Its categories are orthopaedics, trauma and spine; ophthalmology; audiology; cardiology; interventional radiology; endourology; endoscopy; neuromodulation; perfusion; ablation; minimally invasive surgery; In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR) products and tests; and radiology. Pressure area care is not on that list.
patient-handling.quote: New suppliers cannot be added to an agreed procurement framework, except the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS).
patient-handling.use: The only route the page names for joining mid-term is a DPS, and the Innovation DPS categories it lists do not include pressure area care.

patient-handling.org: Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
patient-handling.title: Lease of Mattresses (C468662)
patient-handling.fact: Medstrom Ltd was awarded a seven-year lease of mattresses, pumps and cushions, £900,320.05 excluding VAT, with the award criterion given as price and one tender received. The notice records the procedure as award without prior publication, citing extreme urgency, and explains that the trust chose the supplier because the products are compatible with the trust's own products, as a direct award under the HTE framework (as the notice names it). It also says this is not a capital purchase: invoices are paid annually.
patient-handling.quote: Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust will be leasing these products over a 7 year period.
patient-handling.use: Lease rather than capital, and compatibility with the trust's current beds is the stated reason. Seven years is a long commitment, and bed compatibility is the first objection a new support surface will meet.

patient-handling.title: Bed Frames, Therapeutic Mattresses & Cushions
patient-handling.fact: Call-off from a framework agreement awarded to Arjo UK Limited for the supply of bed frames, therapeutic mattresses and cushions for pressure relief, £928,290 (VAT basis not stated), running 1 August 2025 to 31 January 2027. The notice does not name the framework.
patient-handling.quote: Supply of Bed Frames, Therapeutic Mattresses & Cushions pressure relief
patient-handling.use: Ends 31/01/2027, so what replaces it at Leeds is a live question now.

patient-handling.org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
patient-handling.title: Pressure ulcers: prevention and management (CG179)
patient-handling.fact: Covers risk assessment, prevention and treatment for children, young people and adults at risk of, or with, a pressure ulcer, in secondary and tertiary care and in primary care, community care and emergency departments. On mattresses its recommendations say: use a high-specification foam mattress for adults admitted to secondary care or assessed as high risk in primary and community care (1.1.13); for adults with a pressure ulcer, use high-specification foam and, if that is not sufficient to redistribute pressure, consider a dynamic support surface (1.4.9); do not use standard-specification foam for adults with a pressure ulcer (1.4.10). Adults at high risk should change position at least every 4 hours (1.1.9). NICE last reviewed the guideline on 30 November 2018 and found no new evidence affecting the recommendations.
patient-handling.quote: We have found no new evidence that affects the recommendations.
patient-handling.use: Recommendation 1.4.9 is the line for any dynamic or moving mattress: NICE says to consider a dynamic support surface when high-specification foam is not enough for someone with a pressure ulcer.

patient-handling.org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
patient-handling.title: Pressure ulcers (QS89)
patient-handling.fact: Eight quality statements: risk assessment in hospitals and care homes with nursing, risk assessment by community nursing services, reassessment, skin assessment, advice on repositioning, help with repositioning, information on preventing pressure ulcers, and pressure redistribution devices (statement 8). Statement 9, on medical device-related pressure ulcers, is a placeholder. It applies in England and Wales.
patient-handling.use: Statement 8 is the measurable standard a trust's mattress and cushion provision can be audited against.

patient-handling.title: Implementing the pressure ulcer framework in local reporting systems and reporting to NRLS
patient-handling.date: Not dated on the document (held in NHS England's September 2021 uploads)
patient-handling.fact: A guide for tissue viability nurses and pressure ulcer prevention leads on putting the 'Pressure ulcers: revised definition and measurement framework' into local incident reporting. The recommendations it lists include: the Department of Health and Social Care definition of avoidable/unavoidable should not be used; the 72-hour rule should be abandoned; pressure ulcers of grade 2 and above (the guide's wording) present on admission, and unstageable ulcers, should be included in local monitoring; moisture-associated skin damage should be counted alongside. Where pressure-relieving equipment failed or was unavailable but no ulcer occurred, the incident is reported under a separate listing, not as a medical device related pressure ulcer. It is written for the National Reporting and Learning System (NRLS); whether NRLS is still the national route was not verified here.
patient-handling.quote: Pressure ulcer categories should not be linked to a specific preset degree of harm
patient-handling.use: How a trust counts pressure harm, which is the baseline a business case for a new surface has to move.

patient-handling.title: Cohort study evaluating the burden of wounds to the UK's National Health Service in 2017/2018: update from 2012/2013
patient-handling.fact: Estimates, from a sample of 3,000 patients' records, 202,000 recorded pressure ulcers in 2017/18, equivalent to 0.4% of the adult population. The annual NHS cost of managing all wounds was £8.3 billion, 81% of it incurred in the community. The healing rate of pressure ulcers was 43% higher, in relative terms, than in 2012/13, and patients with a pressure ulcer had a nursing visit or dressing change every 3 to 4 days. A pressure-ulcer-only cost figure was not checked here.
patient-handling.quote: There were an estimated 202 000 recorded pressure ulcers in the study year
patient-handling.use: A citable national volume (2017/18) for the cost-of-problem and frequency lines of a value case.

patient-handling.org: National Pressure Injury Advisory Panel (NPIAP), European Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel (EPUAP) and Pan Pacific Pressure Injury Alliance (PPPIA)
patient-handling.title: Prevention and Treatment of Pressure Ulcers/Injuries: Clinical Practice Guideline (online edition)
patient-handling.date: Quick Reference Guide marked final version September 2026
patient-handling.ends: Online guideline in Beta mode, regularly updated
patient-handling.fact: The online guideline is in Beta mode; the site says it regularly updates content and functionality. It has chapters on repositioning and mobilisation, full body support surfaces, pressure injuries in seated individuals, and technologies to assess skin and tissue. The Quick Reference Guide is marked as the final version of September 2026. Over 200 contributors from more than 40 countries.
patient-handling.quote: The online guideline is in Beta mode.
patient-handling.use: The support surfaces and repositioning chapters are the evidence base any powered or moving surface claim will be tested against.

patient-handling.title: Prevention and management of pressure ulcers standards
patient-handling.fact: Apply across health and social care in Scotland to anyone at risk of, or with, a pressure ulcer, including primary and secondary care, hospices, independent clinics, care at home and care homes. The standards cover organisational leadership, staff education and training, information for people, initial risk assessment at admission or first contact, regular reassessment and a person-centred care plan.
patient-handling.quote: An initial risk assessment is undertaken as part of admission to, or first contact with, a care service to inform care planning.
patient-handling.use: Scotland's counterpart to NICE QS89, and it reaches care at home and care homes.

patient-handling.org: Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
patient-handling.title: Bariatric Equipment Rental
patient-handling.fact: Arjo UK Limited was awarded the rental of bariatric equipment under the competitive flexible procedure: £465,549.60 excluding VAT (£558,659.52 including VAT), running 11 January 2027 to 10 January 2030. The notice does not list the equipment covered.
patient-handling.use: Bariatric equipment bought as a rental, not a capital purchase, and held by Arjo at this trust until January 2030. The same trust leases its mattresses from Medstrom, so its moving and handling and pressure care spend do not sit with one supplier.

patient-handling.org: Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
patient-handling.title: Hoist Maintenance, Service and Ad Hoc Repairs
patient-handling.fact: Open tender run by Synchronicity Care Ltd on the trust's behalf for planned maintenance, statutory Lifting Operations and Lifting Equipment Regulations (LOLER) examinations and reactive repairs on lifting equipment and patient handling accessories. Two 6-monthly service visits across all sites, one annual LOLER weight test, one annual LOLER visual inspection, two 6-monthly patient sling examinations, and Monday to Friday breakdown call-out. £120,000 excluding VAT (£150,000 including VAT), contract period 1 October 2026 to 30 September 2029. Winner not verified: no award notice was on the record when read on 04/11/2026.
patient-handling.use: Shows how one trust specifies hoist servicing, with the sling examinations and the two LOLER visits set out separately. Useful for anyone selling hoists with a service contract, because this is what the service has to cover.

patient-handling.title: Hoist and Rail Systems for Dunkery Ward
patient-handling.fact: Gulmann Ltd was awarded 16 GH3+ hoist systems and 16 XY rail systems, including installation and removal of the old equipment, for £159,252.06. The notice records this as a direct award through the NHS Supply Chain Pressure Area Care and Patient Handling framework (2020/S 129-318007). It does not state a contract end date.
patient-handling.use: Old equipment on one ward replaced with 16 overhead hoist and rail systems, bought by direct award through the national framework rather than a tender.

patient-handling.org: North East London NHS Foundation Trust
patient-handling.title: Delivery and supply of 11 Hoists
patient-handling.fact: Invited quotations for 11 new mobile patient hoists for an inpatient setting, delivered to Orsett Hospital: transfers between beds, chairs and wheelchairs, a base suitable for use beneath low beds, a powered lifting system and a minimum safe working load of 130 kg. £40,000 excluding VAT (£50,000 including VAT), below threshold, open competition. Contract period 3 November to 3 December 2026. Winner not verified: no award notice was on the record when read on 04/11/2026.
patient-handling.use: A current trust specification for mobile hoists, in the trust's own words. The low-bed base and the 130 kg minimum are the points a competing hoist has to meet.

patient-handling.org: Gloucestershire Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust
patient-handling.title: Liko Golvo 9000 Hoist with Lithium Battery
patient-handling.fact: Medaco Ltd was awarded the supply of Liko Golvo 9000 hoists with lithium battery for Charlton Lane and Wotton Lawn: £16,063.21 excluding VAT (£19,275.85 including VAT), below threshold and without competition. Contract period 22 September 2026 to 21 September 2027. The notice does not state the number of hoists.
patient-handling.use: A named model bought below threshold without competition. A purchase like this is settled by the trust before any notice appears: this one was published after signing, so the notice is a competitor signal rather than an opportunity.

patient-handling.org: South Western Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust
patient-handling.title: Ambulance Specialist Manual Handling Training and Consultancy (SWAST-5136-COR)
patient-handling.fact: Pristine Condition International Ltd was appointed for specialist manual handling training, advice, consultancy and a train-the-trainer approach, for operational and non-operational staff across Bristol, Cornwall, Devon, Dorset, Gloucestershire, Somerset and Wiltshire. £75,729.00 excluding VAT (£90,874.80 including VAT), below threshold, open competition.
patient-handling.use: The provider now training this ambulance trust's manual handling trainers. Worth knowing before pitching handling equipment or training to the trust.

patient-handling.title: How the Lifting Operations and Lifting Equipment Regulations apply to health and social care (HSIS4, rev 1)
patient-handling.fact: Sets out which equipment counts as lifting equipment under the Lifting Operations and Lifting Equipment Regulations 1998 (LOLER). Mobile and ceiling hoists, stand and raising aids, slings, bath hoists, bath lifts, lifting platforms and stair lifts all do, with a thorough examination at intervals of 6 months or less, or under a written scheme. Standing transfer aids, recliner baths, riser recliner chairs, profiling beds and trolleys, pillow risers, active mattresses, mattress elevators and lifting cushions do not, but must still be maintained under the Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998 (PUWER). LOLER does not apply to equipment a member of the public buys for use at home, or to equipment on loan solely for use by the individual, family or unpaid carers.
patient-handling.quote: In December 2012, this information sheet was revised to provide further clarity on the various types of stand/transfer aids.
patient-handling.use: The table a moving and handling lead works from. Whether a product falls under LOLER decides whether it brings a 6-monthly examination cost, which belongs in any whole-life cost comparison. Slings count separately as lifting accessories.

patient-handling.title: Getting to grips with hoisting people (HSIS3)
patient-handling.fact: Covers fixed, mobile and overhead hoists. Lists how people fall during hoisting, including the wrong sling size or type, a hoist and sling that are incompatible, poor maintenance, and inappropriate laundering. States that sling sizes and coding vary between manufacturers, and tells readers to follow the manufacturer's advice and refer compatibility concerns to the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA). Calls for an individual handling plan naming the equipment, techniques, number of handlers and sling loops. Accident figures in the sheet are for 2001 to 2007, so they are not current.
patient-handling.use: Sling and hoist compatibility is the regulator's named risk, so a claim that a sling works across hoist brands should come with evidence. A rep should expect the question.

patient-handling.title: Manual handling at work
patient-handling.fact: Employers must avoid hazardous manual handling so far as reasonably practicable, assess the risk of injury from any that cannot be avoided, and reduce that risk to as low as reasonably practicable. The law does not set specific weight limits.
patient-handling.quote: The weight of a load is important, though the law does not set specific weight limits.
patient-handling.use: The legal duty behind buying handling aids. A product case can rest on reducing risk under this duty, and should not rest on a legal weight limit, because there is none.

digital-and-medical-it.org: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)
digital-and-medical-it.title: AI Airlock Phase 3: call for applications open
digital-and-medical-it.fact: The MHRA's regulatory sandbox for artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled medical devices opened its third phase on 6 October 2026, with applications made through the Phase 3 application form on the page. No closing date is given on the page. Phase 2 completed in May 2026 with 7 innovators across 3 regulatory challenges. The government response of the same day gives an applicant webinar on 22 October.
digital-and-medical-it.quote: The MHRA announced on 6th October 2026 the launch of the third phase of the AI Airlock.
digital-and-medical-it.use: The named route for an AI-enabled device maker to test a regulatory question with the regulator before market. Cohort members named on the MHRA's cohort pages are companies with an active regulatory conversation.

digital-and-medical-it.title: Digital Technology Assessment Criteria (DTAC): refreshed form; previous form retired from 6 April 2026
digital-and-medical-it.fact: NHS England's refreshed DTAC form has a 25% reduction in questions and is de-duplicated with the Data Security and Protection Toolkit (DSPT) and the pre-acquisition questionnaire. The page states the previous version of the form should not be used from 6 April 2026 onwards. DTAC covers clinical safety, data protection, technical security, interoperability, and usability and accessibility. Page last edited 21 September 2026.
digital-and-medical-it.quote: The previous version of the DTAC form should not be used from 6 April 2026 onwards.
digital-and-medical-it.use: The assurance form an NHS buyer in England asks a digital health supplier to complete. A supplier still sending the pre-April 2026 form is sending one the owner has retired.

digital-and-medical-it.org: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) and ministers
digital-and-medical-it.title: Government accepts all 44 recommendations of the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare
digital-and-medical-it.fact: On 6 October 2026 the government confirmed it will accept all 44 recommendations of the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare (published 10 September). The MHRA is committed to issue draft guidance by December 2026 on a new approach to managing changes to artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled medical devices, and will begin next year by consulting on how to qualify and classify AI-enabled devices.
digital-and-medical-it.quote: confirmed it will accept all 44 recommendations made by the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare
digital-and-medical-it.use: The dated regulatory timetable for AI-enabled devices: draft change-management guidance by December 2026, then a qualification and classification consultation.

digital-and-medical-it.kind: Innovation partner seeking NHS development partners
digital-and-medical-it.title: Malue: decision support tools for healthcare, looking for NHS development partners
digital-and-medical-it.fact: Malue is an early-stage start-up building decision support tools for healthcare. Its platform gathers the experience of people across healthcare, including industry, procurement, clinicians, leadership and patients, and turns it into trend analyses, summaries and recommendations for the people making decisions. The aim is to help a product or a new pathway move from idea through to adoption, so that work done in one trust does not have to be repeated from scratch in the next. Malue is looking for NHS development partners to help shape the platform. Wording agreed with Lucy Chatwin of Malue, 29 October 2026.
digital-and-medical-it.quote: Malue is an early-stage start-up focused on providing Decision Support Tools to healthcare everywhere.
digital-and-medical-it.use: For an NHS organisation that wants to help shape a decision support platform, or an industry team that wants its product experience captured and shared. Website: malue.co.uk.

colorectal-gi-and-endoscopy.org: Joint Advisory Group on GI Endoscopy (JAG)
colorectal-gi-and-endoscopy.title: JAG accreditation programme and National Endoscopy Database (NED)
colorectal-gi-and-endoscopy.fact: JAG is the accreditation programme for endoscopy services in the UK and Republic of Ireland (ROI), and its site carries the credit '© JAG 2026 by the Royal College of Physicians'. Its participating-services page lists 511 services: 209 accredited, 34 deferred, 26 not awarded, 35 undergoing JAG onsite assessment and 207 undergoing self-assessment or not assessed, with 384 in England. The National Endoscopy Database (NED) is populated by data extracted automatically from the endoscopy reporting system (ERS) at services in the UK. JAG Insourcing, a new accreditation offer for insourced endoscopy providers, launched on 26 October 2026, with the full assessment pathway opening in 2027.
colorectal-gi-and-endoscopy.quote: Joint Advisory Group on GI Endoscopy (JAG) is the accreditation programme for endoscopy services in the UK and ROI.
colorectal-gi-and-endoscopy.use: The participating-services list is the target list for endoscopy: each listed service is in the JAG programme, and its endoscopy reporting system feeds NED, so a reporting supplier's NED upload is part of what a service is relying on.

sterile-services.title: Health Technical Memorandum 01-01: Management and decontamination of surgical instruments (medical devices) used in acute care
sterile-services.date: First published 20 March 2013; all five parts last updated 8 July 2016; publication page updated 26 January 2024
sterile-services.ends: No review or expiry date printed
sterile-services.fact: The national guidance a sterile services department is run to in England. It is published in five parts: Part a management and provision (59 pages), Part b common elements (46 pages), Part c steam sterilization (99 pages), Part d washer-disinfectors (108 pages) and Part e alternatives to steam for the sterilization of reusable medical devices. Parts c and d are the two a capital equipment conversation turns on: the steriliser and the washer-disinfector each have their own part, with their own validation and testing requirements. NHS England classifies it under Topic: Estates, Publication type: Guidance.
sterile-services.quote: Health Technical Memorandum (HTM) 01-01 explains the management of decontamination and the various ways to sterilize reusable medical devices used in acute care.
sterile-services.use: Quote the part, not the memorandum. A buyer who asks what standard a washer-disinfector is validated to is asking about Part d; a steriliser question is Part c. The document is guidance published by NHS England, not a contract or a framework, and it applies in England only - Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland publish their own. It says nothing about who supplies the equipment, so it is never evidence that a company is approved.

sterile-services.title: Health Technical Memorandum 01-06: Decontamination of flexible endoscopes
sterile-services.date: First published 20 March 2013; all five parts last updated 30 June 2016; publication page updated 26 January 2024
sterile-services.ends: No review or expiry date printed
sterile-services.fact: The separate memorandum for flexible endoscope reprocessing, which is why an endoscopy decontamination tender is not an HTM 01-01 tender. Published in five parts: Part A policy and management (31 pages), Part B design and installation (37 pages), Part C operational management (72 pages), Part D validation and verification, including storage and drying cabinets (49 pages) and Part E testing methods (55 pages). Part D is the one that brings the drying cabinet inside the standard alongside the Automated Endoscope Reprocessor (AER).
sterile-services.quote: The guidance consists of 5 parts: policy and management design and installation operational management validation and verification (including storage/drying cabinets) testing methods
sterile-services.use: An Automated Endoscope Reprocessor (AER), its water testing and its drying cabinet all sit under this memorandum, not under HTM 01-01. Trusts that centralise endoscopy decontamination buy against it. England only, and it is guidance rather than a buying route.

sterile-services.title: The decontamination Health Technical Memoranda, and which ones are NOT sterile services
sterile-services.fact: NHS England groups four decontamination memoranda together. Two are this department's: HTM 01-01 (surgical instruments in acute care) and HTM 01-06 (flexible endoscopes). Two are NOT, and they are the reason an award search on the word decontamination returns work that belongs elsewhere: HTM 01-04 covers decontamination of linen for health and social care, last updated 9 June 2016, and HTM 01-05 covers decontamination in primary care dental practices, last updated 26 March 2013.
sterile-services.quote: Health Technical Memorandum 01-05: decontamination in primary care dental practices
sterile-services.use: Use this to place a tender before quoting a standard. A dental practice decontamination contract is HTM 01-05 and a laundry contract is HTM 01-04; neither is a sterile services department buying washer-disinfectors, and treating them as the same patch is the commonest way this market gets mis-sized.

rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.org: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire Integrated Care Board
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.title: Wheelchair and Postural Services, North Yorkshire and York, awarded to Blatchford Limited
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.fact: Blatchford Limited is the named supplier on the award for Wheelchair and Postural Services for North Yorkshire and York. The ICB ran an open procedure under The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023, with a tender value of £15,250,000. The notice records no contract start or end date and no award value, so the term is not verified.
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.quote: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire Integrated Care Board (ICB), hereafter the Relevant Authority, is seeking to commission Wheelchair and Postural Services for North Yorkshire and York through a Competitive Process under The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023.
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.use: Names the incumbent for wheelchairs and postural seating across North Yorkshire and York, and the size of the service at £15.25m. A supplier selling seating or postural equipment into this patch sells through Blatchford, not to the ICB.

rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.title: Integrated Clinical Mobility Service (Wheelchairs and Orthotics) in Northamptonshire, awarded to Blatchford Limited
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.fact: Blatchford Limited is the named supplier on the award for a countywide all-age integrated orthotics, wheelchair and posture service in Northamptonshire. The notice records the procedure as an award procedure without prior publication of a call for competition. No value, start date or end date is given on the notice, so none of those is verified.
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.quote: Provision of a countywide all age integrated high quality, responsive and safe orthotics, wheelchair and posture service that maximises mobility and independence through timely access to both initial assessment and review of individual need, including the provision, and ongoing repair or maintenance where required, of appropriate clinically identified equipment.
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.use: Orthotics and wheelchairs are commissioned together here, under one provider, and awarded without competition. A rep covering Northamptonshire has one door, Blatchford, for both product groups.

rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.org: NHS Black Country Integrated Care Board
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.title: Dudley Wheelchair Assessment and Equipment Service, awarded to AJM Healthcare
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.ends: 30/09/2029, option to extend up to a further 2 years
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.fact: AJM Healthcare holds the Wheelchair Assessment and Equipment Service for patients registered with a Dudley GP. The award records £6,749,999 against an above-threshold open procedure, running three years from 1 October 2026 to 30 September 2029, with the Commissioner holding an option to extend for up to a further two years. The award entity is recorded both as AJM Healthcare and as AJM Healthcare Group Limited.
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.quote: As a result of this above threshold open procedure process, a Contract has been entered into with the Most Advantageous Tender supplier for a period of 3 Years commencing on 01st October 2026, with the Commissioner having the option to extend the contract for up to a further 2 years.
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.use: The Dudley service changed hands with effect from 1 October 2026. Any wheelchair or postural product going into Dudley now goes through AJM Healthcare, and the first re-let point is autumn 2029.

rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.org: Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.title: Specialist Mobility and Rehabilitation Centre wheelchair maintenance and refurbishment, awarded to AJM Healthcare
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.fact: A J Mobility Limited, trading as AJM Healthcare, holds wheelchair maintenance and refurbishment for the trust's Specialist Mobility and Rehabilitation Centre, covering Lancashire and South Cumbria. The award value is £10,150,000 against a tender value of £10,500,000, and the contract period runs 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2032. The procedure is recorded as a competitive flexible procedure.
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.quote: Wheelchair maintenance and refurbishment services for LSC
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.use: Maintenance and refurbishment is a separate five-year contract from assessment and supply, and it is already let to 2032. Taken with Dudley, it shows AJM Healthcare holding both service and maintenance work in two unconnected patches.

rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.org: Business Services Organisation, Procurement and Logistics Service (PaLS)
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.title: Postural Management Equipment and Accessories framework for Northern Ireland
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.fact: PaLS awarded a Northern Ireland framework for the supply and delivery of postural management equipment and accessories through an open procedure, running 1 November 2026 to 31 October 2030. The tender value is £26,000,000 and each of the eight lot awards records £3,170,000. Ten suppliers appear across the lots: Accora (Ireland) Ltd, BES Healthcare Ltd, Evolution Healthcare, James Leckey Design, John Preston & Co (Belfast) Ltd, LC Seating Limited, Moorings Mediquip UK Ltd, Primacy Healthcare 21 Ltd, Sync Living Ltd and Primacy Healthcare 21 Limited as a second recorded entity. No single supplier appears on all eight lots.
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.quote: Business Services Organisation (BSO), Procurement and Logistics Service (PaLS) sought through this tender opportunity to establish a Framework for the for the supply and delivery of Postural Management Equipment and Accessories
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.use: The national route into Northern Ireland for postural seating until October 2030, and the lot pattern says which competitor can sell what there. A supplier not on it has no PaLS route for four years.

rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.title: Orthotics Products and Services including Prosthetic Services framework: the route trusts use, and its end date
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.fact: The NHS SBS portfolio dated 30/06/2026 lists the Orthotics Products and Services including Prosthetic Services Framework Agreement with a maximum end date of 08/10/2027 and says it covers stock, modular and bespoke products across nine lots for upper and lower body orthoses for adult and paediatric patients. The Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital award notice describes the same framework (reference SBS10247) as three lots: orthotic products, orthotic services and prosthetic services. The portfolio does not name the suppliers on each lot, and the nine-lot and three-lot descriptions are not reconciled here: the supplier list per lot is not verified.
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.quote: The Orthotics Products and Services including Prosthetic Services Framework Agreement allows for the provision of stock, modular and bespoke products. Nine lots cover upper and lower body orthoses for adult and paediatric patients.
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.use: Names the national route for orthotic and prosthetic buying and the date it runs out. A trust buying through a further competition (as RNOH did) is buying under this framework, so a supplier outside it needs to be on the re-let. Get the lot and supplier list from NHS SBS before quoting it to a customer.

rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.org: Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.title: Provision of Prosthetic and Orthotic Services, awarded to Hugh Steeper Limited (t/a Steeper) under NHS SBS SBS10247
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.fact: Hugh Steeper Limited (t/a Steeper) is the named supplier, the only one on the notice, after a further competition under the NHS SBS Orthotics Products and Services including Prosthetic Services framework (reference SBS10247). Three bids were received. The contract value is £6,369,486.54 and it was signed on 03/09/2026. The trust awarded one contract to one supplier covering all three lots. The notice describes the full term as seven years with two optional 12-month extensions; no start or end date is recorded on the notice, so the end date is not verified. The notice's lot record carries the status 'cancelled' while the award and contract are 'active'; what that status means is not verified.
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.quote: The Authority will award a single contract to a single supplier covering all three (3) Lots.
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.use: The RNOH prosthetic, orthotic products and orthotic services spend sits with one supplier for the seven-year term, so a rep selling orthotic devices or prosthetic components here sells through Steeper, not to the trust.

rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.org: Ministry of Defence (Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre)
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.title: Prosthetics and Orthotics Rehabilitation Service at DMRC: four-year contract from 01/04/2027, tender closed
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.fact: The Ministry of Defence published an open-procedure tender for an on-site prosthetic and orthotic rehabilitation service at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre, estimated at £8,736,000 excluding VAT (£10,100,000 including VAT). The contract period runs 01/04/2027 to 31/03/2031 with an option to extend by up to 24 months to 31/03/2033. Award weighting is 50% cost and 50% technical. Tenders closed on 07/10/2026. The record carries no award, so the winning supplier is not verified. The contractor must supply its own prosthetic and orthotic management IT system.
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.quote: The authority is seeking to tender for a 4 -year contract to start on 01 Apr 2027, with the option to extend up to 24 months.
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.use: A live prosthetic and orthotic service contract of about £8.7m ex VAT starting 01/04/2027, with the winner not yet on the record. Watch Find a Tender for the award; the contractor must also supply a prosthetic and orthotic management IT system, which is a possible route for a digital supplier.

rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.org: The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust, with RJAH and Shropshire Community Health NHS Trust
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.title: Orthotic Splints and Braces: joint tender for 2027, closed 13/11/2026
rehabilitation-prosthetics-and-orthotics.fact: Three Shropshire-area buyers (Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital, the Robert Jones and Agnes Hunt Orthopaedic Hospital and Shropshire Community Health) are named on one below-threshold open tender, valued at £60,135.88 excluding VAT, for a contract period of 01/01/2027 to 31/12/2027. It estimates 55,000 to 60,000 people in England with amputation or limb difference, with about 25,000 seen by prosthetic services each year, and a catchment of 1 to 2 million people per specialist prosthetic centre. Every service must have an on-site workshop to fabricate, repair and maintain prostheses. The only named outcome metric is a Socket Comfort Score of 7 or more on delivery of a new socket. High activity and competitive sport prostheses are not routinely commissioned. Microprocessor knees and multi-grip hands are governed by separate clinical commissioning policies. mental-health.fact: PCMIS Health Technologies Ltd is the named supplier on a below-threshold award made without competition, value GBP 18,340 excluding VAT (GBP 22,008 gross), signed 05/08/2026, running 01/10/2026 to 31/03/2027. The record describes the scope as the PCMIS licence with maintenance, support, hosting, SMS appointment reminders and online e-referral. Which services use it beyond City and Hackney Talking Therapies is not verified.
mental-health.quote: Provision of PCMIS system licence providing maintenance, support, hosting, sms patient appointment reminders, online e-referral
mental-health.use: City and Hackney Talking Therapies run their patient record and e-referral on PCMIS, a six-month licence due to end 31/03/2027, so a replacement or add-on digital tool would come up for decision around then. Renewal intent is not verified.
